ledger_text: 3. **The stance tables (dmg 0.9/1.2/1.4, reach 300/200/100) are MASTERY-9 CEILING values, not base.**
text: The mastery ceiling question is closed by data, not arithmetic alone. skilldata.xml skill id 1000 has displayname 6000, which strings.json resolves to 'Light Stance Mastery', is marked <passive>1</passive>, and carries exactly ten <level> blocks with <value> 1 through 10 (required 1..9). StatsManager.as:740-742 seeds skillStats with IntStat(1000,1)/(1001,1)/(1002,1), so mastery is 1-indexed with floor 1 and cap 10. Feeding 10 into §1t99s0§.as:3262 gives exactly 0.90 and into :3265 exactly 1.20 — the ledger's own ceiling numbers. There is no off-by-one here, unlike the DAN stat which really is stored 0-indexed.

text: The in-battle stance switch is a first-class UI affordance, not just a hotkey. Web §1t113s0§ (BattleUI) declares the button §1t5158s0§ at :22, gives it buttonMode at :149, labels it §1t5161s0§.text = getString(208) = 'Change Stance' at :146, and hit-tests it at :379-381 into §1t5207s0§ (:468-480), which cycles the stance when §1t4470s0§() passes and plays Snd_error when it does not. Android BattleUI.as:109-110 carries the same `changestancelabel.text = LangManager.getString(208)`, so the button is in BOTH builds — this is not a v0.717 addition. The android twin also decodes three obfuscated web fields: BattleUI.as:101-102 `crittext.text = getString(175)` == §1t113s0§.as:120-121 (field declared :44), so §1t5169s0§ = crittext, §1t5161s0§ = changestancelabel, and §1t5182s0§ = reloadbar (declared BattleUI.as:60).

text: THE FRAME WINS, AND IT OVERTURNS A MEASUREMENT DOC. Three video-study segment notes describe this HUD element wrongly and the ledger inherited the error. docs/research/video-study/segments/B-11-castle-gate-lever-puzzle.md:7 calls the label 'Yellow text'; :45 and :71 read the slot as 'a green X/20 bar (stance-lock resource, label CANNOT CHANGE STANCE)' fluctuating 4/20 -> 2/20 -> 3/20; docs/research/video-study/segments/A-16-beach-fights-named-enemy-jinbei-archer.md:23 calls it a 'blue bar ... 20/20'. The frame shows otherwise: in t1003.000.png the CANNOT CHANGE STANCE label is PALE GREY, distinctly not the saturated yellow of the '150% DAMAGE' line directly beneath it, and its bar carries NO numerals at all - the numeric bars are the green HP (14/20) and blue Chi (31/31) ABOVE it. The notes conflated the third bar with the HP bar and the label colour with the buff banner's. The code agrees with the frame: §1t113s0§.as:111 builds the label at '#BBBBBB', and §1t5205s0§ sets only bar.scaleX with no text, while the numeric bars are set by §1t5202s0§ at :319-324.

text: The war-map board specification is NOT android-only, which was the one real hole in the packet's world finding. Web v0.717 §1t7934s0§.as:15/:17/:19 declare 8 / 21 / 51 — byte-identical to WarSelectUI.as — :232 is the land test `getPixel(param1 + §1t12536s0§ - §1t12535s0§, param2 + §1t12537s0§) != 0`, and :299-300 place the war flag at `(x + 21) * 10 + 4.5` / `(y + 51) * 10 + 8.8`. §1t6481s0§.as:17/:19/:21 repeats the same three constants for the world map. The 63x72 mask itself is web bindata 92 (reference/extracted/bindata/92_1t4648s0.bin), not an android blob. So the C2 build-parity caveat does not apply to the war map: geography, bounds, offsets and pitch are all attested on the WEB side.

text: A genuine, non-circular web/android parity datum - rare in this corpus, and it survives correction C2. reference/extracted/bindata/92_1t4648s0.bin (a WEB payload bindata file) and reference/extracted/android/110_Mobile_MapBitmapData.bin (the ANDROID blob) have the identical md5 13068dfa1a5cc5628720a25782f93fed. Both are a GIF89a 63x72 with exactly 735 white and 3801 black pixels. C2's circularity warning does not apply here, because 92 is a web-side artifact and 110 is android-side - this is not a file diffed against itself. Android WarSelectUI.as:153 wires it to the war board via QuestEngine.getMapBitmapData(), and Mobile_MapBitmapData.as:5 embeds 110 by name, so the file's role is named by the game, not inferred.
